about: Every number is {value, source}, with a link when it comes from a page. source is 'measured' (on the creator's DGX Spark), 'reported' (published by someone else: a spec sheet, a manual or a benchmark; link says where) or 'estimated' (our own formula or placeholder; note says how). Units: memGB and reserveGB in GB, bw in GB/s, tflops in TFLOPS of 16-bit matrix math. memGB minus reserveGB is what a model may use. The Strix Halo also lists the specs its interior (machines/strixhalo.js) is drawn from.

system.value: AMD Ryzen AI Halo developer platform, a mini PC with the Ryzen AI Max+ 395 and 128 GB: 150 x 150 x 45.4 mm

memGB.note: Max. Memory 128 GB; the developer platform ships with 128 GB

memType.note: System Memory Type 256-bit LPDDR5x, Max Memory Speed LPDDR5x-8000

busBits.note: drawn as 8 lanes of 32 bits, one per memory package, like the Spark

gpuMemLinuxDefaultGB.note: Linux lets the GPU map about half of RAM by default (the GTT limit); AMD's example: 62.82 GB of 125.65 GB

gpuMemLinuxMaxGB.note: the usual setup for local AI raises the limit with ttm.pages_limit=31457280 (120 GiB in 4 KiB pages) and a 512 MB BIOS frame buffer; AMD's own tool for it is amd-ttm (ROCm docs above)

reserveGB.note: memGB minus gpuMemLinuxMaxGB: what Linux keeps when the GPU may map 120 GiB

tflops.note: 40 CUs x 2,900 MHz x 512 16-bit matrix operations per CU per clock; the 512 is RDNA 3's rate from the RX 7900 XTX (96 CUs, 2,500 MHz, 123 TFLOPs FP16 matrix)

cpu.value: 16 Zen 5 cores on two chiplets; 3 dies in the package
cpu.note: Package Die Count 3: two CPU chiplets and the I/O die that holds the GPU, the NPU and the memory controllers

npuTops.note: XDNA 2 NPU; llama.cpp runs on the GPU and leaves it idle

powerW.note: the developer platform's TDP; the chip itself runs at 45-120 W, 55 W by default (AMD spec page)

ports.value: 3 USB-C, 1 USB-C power input, 10 Gbps Ethernet, HDMI 2.1b
